key_entities: untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge
propositions: Compaction leaves the tracker working tree dirty (untracked SNAPSHOT.json, *.retired, .tmp-event-*) when the detached background sweep is interrupted before commit.

The next reconverge union-merge runs git merge origin/tickets; a peer's pushed .retired/SNAPSHOT paths must be created but already exist untracked in the working tree, causing git merge to abort with 'untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge'.

Push recovery cannot clear untracked files (git reset --hard is tracked-only; git stash without -u omits them), so every reconverge retry re-aborts identically, permanently wedging the store and stranding local commits off origin.

The self-heal fix relocates only the exact untracked paths named by git's error message into a quarantine directory outside the worktree, then retries the merge once; on success, both parents are kept and no local commit is orphaned.
Genuine content conflicts still abort and hint rebar fsck-recover (unchanged); .tmp-event-* and any untracked path not named by git are left untouched.

Pre-existing tracked .archived deletions remain after worker death and cause plan-review/completion gates to fail on dirty git status checks; durable remediation requires untracking .archived from HEAD via git rm --cached and adding git checkout/clean cleanup on compaction-worker death.
